title: A database that outgrows what the live event log justifies, live or a test database (the gates' or the fleet's), raises an alert, and storage names the test databases' schemas
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs (the alert step's readings, `open_keys`, how an alert fires and clears), crates/spawn-postgres/src/fleet.rs (objective 065's `database_storage`), crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (065's `health.storage`) and web/src/resources.ts (065's `storageView`). This objective comes after 065, whose storage report it extends.

The problem. The fleet's test database (spawn_fleet_test, the database the loop hands the engines from SPAWN_FLEET_TEST_DATABASE_URL; the loop's own SPAWN_TEST_DATABASE_URL names the gates' test server) grew to 2.7 GB. It held 2533 schemas that crate tests had created and never dropped (lead, queue.md 11-11 09:37). Nothing measured it and nothing alerted. It was found by hand on the host's disk, and first read as live-database bloat: sync/roadmap-effects.md and 065's prompt still call it that. The lead's read-only SELECTs on the live cluster (2026-11-12) show the live database is 159 MB for a 35 MB event log, with negligible dead tuples. P19 stops that leak at its source, but nothing says when it, or any other cause, makes a database outgrow its data again.

Required behaviour.
(a) Every SPAWN_ALERT_DATABASE_SECS (default 600), the loop's alert step reads:
- the live database's size and its event log's bytes (the sum of spawn_events.kind's stored size, `pg_column_size`);
- the size and schemas (other than pg_*, information_schema and public) of each test database it is given, each when set: the gates' (SPAWN_TEST_DATABASE_URL, role "test") and the engines' (SPAWN_FLEET_TEST_DATABASE_URL, role "fleet_test").
(b) A database at or above SPAWN_ALERT_DATABASE_FLOOR_MB (default 1024) and above SPAWN_ALERT_DATABASE_RATIO (default 10) times the log's bytes opens one `database_size` alert.
- Its subject is "database <name>".
- Its evidence is {database, role ("live", "test" or "fleet_test"), bytes, log_bytes, ratio (bytes over log_bytes, one decimal), schemas}.
- Its text names the database, its size, the ratio and "<n> schemas".
- There is one open alert per database.
(c) It clears at the first reading where the database no longer qualifies, with that reading as its cleared evidence.
(d) `/api/fleet`'s `health.storage` (065) also carries `test_databases`: [{role, name, bytes, schemas}], the gates' first, each only when its URL is set, and `database.log_bytes`. storageView adds a row "Gate test database" and a row "Fleet test database", each with note "<n> schemas", and the "Database" row's note also says "log <size>".

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/074.sh. A real `spawn loop` and `spawn serve` run on a scratch database (the live one) and are given two more scratch databases: the gates' test database (empty) and the fleet's.
- The live database holds about 2 MB of log. It is above the floor (set 1 MB under its own size) but within 10 times the log.
- The fleet test database holds 40 padded schemas, above both the floor and the ratio.
- Then 35 of its schemas are dropped.
Checks:
- (1) The fleet test database has one open `database_size` alert. Its evidence is the database, role "fleet_test", 40 schemas, bytes over the floor and over 10 times log_bytes, and the ratio to one decimal, and its text names the database and "40 schemas". The live database and the gates' test database have none.
- (3) `health.storage.test_databases` is the gates' {role "test", schemas 0} then the fleet's {role "fleet_test", schemas 40}, each with its name and bytes, and `database.log_bytes` is a number. storageView has the "Gate test database" ("0 schemas") and "Fleet test database" ("40 schemas") rows and the log's size in the "Database" note, and no test-database row without them.
- (2) After the drop the alert clears, its cleared evidence showing 5 schemas within 10 times the log.
It fails with 1 on ecb177ab: there is no reading, no alert and no storage line.

The product reason. The disk is the fleet's hard limit, and a database that silently fills it stops every gate. The last time, a test database grew 270-fold and was found by hand and misread as live-database bloat. Measured against the live log, which is what the data justifies, the same leak raises one alert days before it matters, and the storage page says which database and how many schemas.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour:
- alerts.rs unit tests of the reading: under the floor, within the ratio, over both, the clear, one open per database, and an unreachable test database (a line, no alert), each URL unset;
- a spawn-postgres test of the size reading through the real store;
- web/test tests for (d).
